domain: How the psychiatric concept of 'trauma' has come to constitute the very experiences it was invented to measure
topic: How the psychiatric concept of 'trauma' has come to constitute the very experiences it was invented to measure

movement.gist: Present the received clinical picture: trauma studies since the 1980s have identified a consistent constellation of symptoms (intrusive memory, hyperarousal, avoidance) across car crashes, combat, assault — presented as a stable, cross-population discovery about how the mind responds to overwhelming events.

Turn to the instrument: the DSM's Criterion A checklist and the intake questionnaire don't just record trauma, they train clinicians and patients alike to notice, name, and report certain sensations as 'symptoms' — the diagnostic interview is itself an act of teaching people what trauma feels like.

Use one sustained example — a family present at a relative's car-crash resuscitation, one member fluent in trauma-vocabulary (a university lecturer exposed to students' 'traumatized' emails) and one member (the older mother) with no such vocabulary at all — to show the same physiological ordeal producing radically different, instrument-shaped experiences of what happened; the diagnostic category is inseparable from what it finds because who has absorbed it changes what gets felt as trauma.

State the residue: something did happen — broken ribs, a shattered face, a body in intensive care — that no vocabulary invented or dissolved; but exactly which parts of the suffering are 'trauma proper' cannot be read off nature, only off which measuring language a person had already been given before the crash.

primary.axis: trauma as discovered fact of the psyche vs trauma as a diagnostic category that shapes what counts as injury
poles: trauma is a real, measurable wound the instrument merely detects
the diagnostic instrument partly manufactures the boundaries of what counts as trauma

secondary.axis: clinical/narrow use of 'trauma' vs everyday/expansive use of 'trauma'
poles: trauma as a bounded clinical event (DSM criterion A)
trauma as an elastic descriptor for any distressing experience

tension_system.interaction: the everyday expansion of 'trauma' is the visible symptom of the instrument effect: once the clinical category becomes a public vocabulary, the vocabulary starts generating the experiences it names, and the secondary tension becomes the evidence for the primary one

family_realization.note: Passage relentlessly executes Instrument Effect. Paragraph 2 names the mechanism directly: checklist supplies categories, interview teaches sensations, patient learns vocabulary. Paragraphs 3-4 show constitutive work assembling suffering into 'trauma.' Object-level (broken ribs, pounding heart) stays cleanly separated from method-level (which naming gets attached). The difficulty—keeping boundaries sharp while denying fraud—is genuinely sustained.

ending_behavior.note: Paragraph 4's closing delivers Horizon Clause precisely: 'that will hold until the public vocabulary shifts again, as it is shifting now.' Thesis conditions own obsolescence on vocabulary change. 'Reframe displace' stance achieved: the line drawn through suffering gets redrawn. Slight gap: 'one forwarded student email at a time' could hold aperture tighter, but the until-clause is crisp.

voice_consistency.note: Patient Explicator voice throughout. Paragraph 1-2 gently define: 'This is not fraud. It is teaching.' Paragraph 3 performs the generous turn: 'It is tempting to read this as... That reading misses the mechanism.' The knife turns in final third, reframing fragility as vocabulary. No generic AI-essay register; cadence is deliberate, almost clinical.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(A) and (B) are adjacent-answer traps that misread paragraph 3's explicit rejection of generational fragility and paragraph 2's denial of fraud. Q3(A) overshoots into pure construction when the passage holds bodily reality. Q4(B) inverts causality. Q5(D) confuses levels. Q6(C) adopts paragraph 1 framing that paragraphs 2-4 displace. All traps are passage-specific semantic misreadings, not lexical extremity.

explanation_quality.note: Every wrong option is tied to specific passage locations and mechanism names: 'half_truth' distinguishes partial adoption of thesis; 'adjacent_answer' names overshooting into pure construction; 'stance_misread' captures misattribution of author intent. Explanations quote paragraph references and name the constitutive-work mechanism. Zero 'not mentioned' dismissals.

answers.reasoning: Passage insists injury is real but vocabulary determines what's assembled as trauma.
Directly parallels vocabulary shift shaping which distress gets named as condition.
Constitutive work means vocabulary assembles distress into trauma; mother lacks assembly point.
Line can't be read off injury itself implies injury lacks built-in trauma/grief boundary.
Framing questions shape witness reporting, paralleling interview naming sensations in advance.
Author critiques the checklist's boundary-drawing while affirming physical/bodily reality of suffering.
